extracted_factors.Label: Political Turnover and REDD+ Continuity
extracted_factors.Description: The implementation of REDD+ is susceptible to changes in political administration, hindering continuity and progress.

extracted_factors.Label: Institutionalization of REDD+
extracted_factors.Description: REDD+ needs to be embedded in national and regional laws and regulations to ensure its sustainability and effectiveness.

extracted_factors.Label: Socioeconomic and Political Drivers of Deforestation
extracted_factors.Description: Underlying drivers such as agricultural expansion and unclear land rights contribute to deforestation and need addressing for REDD+ to be successful.

extracted_factors.Label: Global Climate Architecture and REDD+
extracted_factors.Description: Global frameworks like the Paris Agreement influence national REDD+ commitments and actions.

extracted_factors.Label: REDD+ Payments for Emission Reductions
extracted_factors.Description: Indonesia's receipt of REDD+ payments for reduced emissions indicates measurable progress in emissions reductions.

extracted_factors.Label: Business-as-Usual Practices
extracted_factors.Description: The persistence of traditional land-use practices that favor deforestation over sustainable conservation efforts.

extracted_pain_points.description: REDD+ initiatives are vulnerable to political changes, which can lead to organizational dissolution or changes in policy priorities.
Insufficient addressing of socioeconomic drivers of deforestation poses a challenge for REDD+ mechanisms.
Weak human and technical capacity for monitoring and reporting REDD+ outcomes at subnational levels.
Unclear land rights and allotments impede REDD+ effectiveness and lead to conflicts.
